arxiv-2011-10142.title: Cooperating RPN’s Improve Few-Shot Object Detection
arxiv-2011-10142.creator: Weilin Zhang, Yu-Xiong Wang, David A. Forsyth
arxiv-2011-10142.description: Abstract Learning to detect an object in an image from very few training examples - few-shot object detection - is challenging, because the classifier that sees proposal boxes has very little training data. A particularly challenging training regime occurs when there are one or two training examples.

arxiv-2012-04236.title: Phase sensitivity approaching quantum Cramér-Rao bound in a modified SU(1,1) interferometer
arxiv-2012-04236.creator: Jian-Dong Zhang, Chenglong You, Chuang Li, Shuai Wang
arxiv-2012-04236.description: Abstract SU(1,1) interferometers, based on the usage of nonlinear elements, are superior to passive interferometers in phase sensitivity. However, the SU(1,1) interferometer cannot make full use of photons carrying phase information as the second nonlinear element annihilates some of the photons inside.

arxiv-2101-07795.title: On the derivation of the Khmaladze transforms Journal: ArXiv
arxiv-2101-07795.creator: Leigh A Roberts
arxiv-2101-07795.description: Abstract Some 40 years ago Khmaladze introduced a transform which greatly facilitated the distribution free goodness of fit testing of statistical hypotheses. In the last decade, he has published a related transform, broadly offering an alternative means to the same end.

arxiv-2108-05176.title: Convergence to a Gaussian by narrowing of central peak in Brownian yet non-Gaussian diffusion in disordered environments
arxiv-2108-05176.creator: Adrian Pacheco-Pozo, Igor M. Sokolov
arxiv-2108-05176.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Adrian Pacheco-Pozo, Igor M. Sokolov. In usual diffusion, the concentration profile, starting from an initial distribution showing sharp features, first gets smooth and then converges to a Gaussian. By considering several examples, we show that the art of convergence to a Gaussian in diffusion in disordered media with infinite contrast may be strikingly different: sharp features of initial distribution do not smooth out at long times. This peculiarity of the strong disorder may be of importance for diagnostics of disorder in complex, e.g.

arxiv-2205-12992.title: Open Arms: Open-Source Arms, Hands & Control
arxiv-2205-12992.creator: David Hanson, Alishba Imran, Gerardo Morales, Vytas Krisciunas, Aditya Sagi, Aman Malali, Rushali Mohbe, Raviteja Upadrashta
arxiv-2205-12992.description: Abstract Open Arms is a novel open-source platform of realistic human-like robotic hands and arms hardware with 28 Degree-of-Freedom (DoF), designed to extend the capabilities and accessibility of humanoid robotic grasping and manipulation. The Open Arms framework includes an open SDK and development environment, simulation tools, and application development tools to build and operate Open Arms.

arxiv-2207-09095.title: Secure Intelligent Reflecting Surface Aided Integrated Sensing and Communication
arxiv-2207-09095.creator: Meng Hua, Qingqing Wu, Wen Chen, Octavia A. Dobre, and A. Lee Swindlehurst
arxiv-2207-09095.description: Abstract In this paper, an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is leveraged to enhance the physical layer security of an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system in which the IRS is deployed to not only assist the downlink communication for multiple users, but also create a virtual line-of-sight (LoS) link for target sensing.

arxiv-2302-03066.title: On the equivalence between the minimax theorem and strong duality of conic linear programming
arxiv-2302-03066.creator: Nikos Dimou
arxiv-2302-03066.description: Abstract We prove the almost equivalence between two-player zero-sum games and conic linear programming problems in reflexive Banach spaces. The previous fundamental results of von Neumann, Dantzig, Adler, and von Stengel on the equivalence between linear programming and finite games with strategy sets defined over ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} , are therefore extended to more general strategy spaces.

Summers, Timothy Carleton, Kevin C. Harrington, Jose M. Diego, Haojing Yan, Anton M. Koekemoer, Christopher N. A. Willmer, Andreea Petric, Lukas J. Furtak, Nic

The long-wavelength filters of JWST ’s NIRCam offer a significant step forward.

arxiv-2406-14708.title: Fermionic dynamical Casimir effect: Magnus expansion
arxiv-2406-14708.creator: C. D. Fosco, G. Hansen
arxiv-2406-14708.description: Abstract We study pair creation out of the vacuum, for a system consisting of a massive Dirac field in 1 + 1 1+1 dimensions, contained between a pair of perfectly reflecting boundaries, one of them oscillating. After analyzing some general properties of the vacuum-decay process, we evaluate the corresponding transition amplitude in a Magnus expansion of the S S -matrix.

arxiv-2409-04081.title: UI-JEPA: Towards Active Perception of User Intent through Onscreen User Activity
arxiv-2409-04081.creator: Yicheng Fu, Raviteja Anantha, Prabal Vashisht, Jianpeng Cheng, Etai Littwin
arxiv-2409-04081.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yicheng Fu, Raviteja Anantha, Prabal Vashisht, Jianpeng Cheng, Etai Littwin. Generating user intent from a sequence of user interface (UI) actions is a core challenge in comprehensive UI understanding. Recent advancements in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have led to substantial progress in this area, but their demands for extensive model parameters, computing power, and high latency makes them impractical for scenarios requiring lightweight, on-device solutions with low latency or heightened privacy.

arxiv-2505-12937.title: Doubling Qubits in a Trapped-Ion System via Vibrational Dual-Rail Encoding
arxiv-2505-12937.creator: Minhyeok Kang, Wentao Chen, Hyukjoon Kwon, Kihwan Kim, Joonsuk Huh
arxiv-2505-12937.description: Abstract Vibrational modes of trapped ions have traditionally served as quantum buses to mediate internal qubits. However, with recent advances in quantum control, it has become possible to use these vibrational modes directly as quantum computational resources, such as bosonic qubits.

arxiv-2506-04465.title: Flare frequency in M dwarfs belonging to Young Moving Groups.
arxiv-2506-04465.creator: E. Mamonova, Y. Shan, A. F. Kowalski, S. Wedemeyer, S. C. Werner
arxiv-2506-04465.description: Abstract Context. M stars are preferred targets for studying terrestrial exoplanets, for which we hope to obtain their atmosphere spectra in the next decade. However, M dwarfs have long been known for strong magnetic activity and the ability to frequently produce optical, broadband emission flares. Aims.

arxiv-2506-24117.title: Intertextual Parallel Detection in Biblical Hebrew: A Transformer-Based Benchmark
arxiv-2506-24117.creator: David M. Smiley
arxiv-2506-24117.description: Abstract Identifying parallel passages in biblical Hebrew (BH) is central to biblical scholarship for understanding intertextual relationships. Traditional methods rely on manual comparison, a labor-intensive process prone to human error. This study evaluates the potential of pre-trained transformer-based language models, including E5, AlephBERT, MPNet, and LaBSE, for detecting textual parallels in the Hebrew Bible.

arxiv-2507-02314.title: MAGIC: Mask-Guided Diffusion Inpainting with Multi-Level Perturbations and Context-Aware Alignment for Few-Shot Anomaly Generation
arxiv-2507-02314.creator: JaeHyuck Choi MinJun Kim JeHyeong Hong, [4pt] Department of Artificial Intelligence Semiconductor Engineering, Hanyang University, Department of Electronic Engineering, Hanyang University [4pt] {sunhp1333, ihatelemon, jhh37}@hanyang.ac.kr
arxiv-2507-02314.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by JaeHyuck Choi MinJun Kim JeHyeong Hong, [4pt] Department of Artificial Intelligence Semiconductor Engineering, Hanyang University, Department of Electronic Engineering, Hanyang University [4pt] {sunhp1333, ihatelemon, jhh37}@hanyang.ac.kr. Few-shot anomaly generation is emerging as a practical solution for augmenting the scarce anomaly data in industrial quality control settings.

arxiv-2511-15193.title: Gravitational Wave Phase shifts of black hole mergers in AGN Disks
arxiv-2511-15193.creator: Hiromichi Tagawa, Connar Rowan, János Takátsy, Lorenz Zwick, Kai Hendriks, Wen-Biao Han, Johan Samsing
arxiv-2511-15193.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hiromichi Tagawa, Connar Rowan, János Takátsy, Lorenz Zwick, Kai Hendriks, Wen-Biao Han, Johan Samsing. Ground-based gravitational wave (GW) detectors have discovered about 200 compact object mergers. The astrophysical origins of these events are highly debated, and it is possible that at least a fraction of them originate from dynamical environments. Among these, the disks of active galactic nuclei (AGN) are particularly interesting as promising environments, as some observed properties may be more readily produced there.

arxiv-2602-13457.title: Inferring Turn-Rate-Limited Engagement Zones with Sacrificial Agents for Safe Trajectory Planning
arxiv-2602-13457.creator: Grant Stagg, Cameron K. Peterson
arxiv-2602-13457.description: Abstract This paper presents a learning-based framework for estimating pursuer parameters in turn-rate-limited pursuit–evasion scenarios using sacrificial agents. Each sacrificial agent follows a straight-line trajectory toward an adversary and reports whether it was intercepted or survived. These binary outcomes are related to the pursuer’s parameters through a geometric reachable-region (RR) model.

pmc-10507972.title: Improving milk donation behavior through an educational intervention based on the theory of planned behavior: study protocol of a cluster randomized controlled trial
pmc-10507972.creator: Shirin Shahbazi Sighaldeh, Maryam Moridi, Vafa Ghorban Sabagh, Anoshirvan Kazemnejad, Fatemeh Shateranni
pmc-10507972.description: BackgroundBreastfeeding mothers’ decisions to donate their milk is influenced by their knowledge, attitudes, and subjective norms such as their family’s opinions on milk donation. In Iran, women have favorable knowledge and positive attitudes toward breastfeeding, but they lack sufficient information and education about milk banks.

pmc-11306279.title: OrganoidPortal: Web server and single‐cell transcriptome database featuring reference atlases of organoids
pmc-11306279.creator: Jialin Chen, Hao Yu, Ke Sui, Hai Fang, Xi Zhang, Zheng Wang
pmc-11306279.description: on the exploration of novel cell types, pathophysiological mechanisms, drug targets, and biomarkers. 3 Here, we present OrganoidPortal (http://organoidportal.jflab.ac.cn:18083/app/organoidportal), a user‐friendly, up‐to‐date and dedicated data resource and versatile web server for the efficient analysis, interpretation, transcriptome profiling and evaluation of organoids. It addresses the deficiencies in existing databases by providing the most comprehensive functionality within its field (Table S1).

pmc-11517341.title: Evaluating the psychological antecedents of vaccination in applicants to primary health care centers
pmc-11517341.creator: C Özbaş, M Tokatlı Doğan, F N Baran Aksakal
pmc-11517341.description: BackgroundVaccine acceptance can be enhanced by understanding the psychological antecedents of vaccination. The 5C model identifies relevant factors: confidence, complacency, constraints, calculation, and collective responsibility. This study aims to evaluate these factors among primary health care center applicants in Ankara.MethodsA total of 1712 individuals aged 18 and over, who visited primary health care centers, participated in the study.

pmc-12517027.title: Predictors, mediators, effect modifiers and preventive actions regarding secondary school teacher burnout, anxiety and depression—protocol for a systematic scoping review
pmc-12517027.creator: Marius König, Jonas P Wallraff, Florian Glenewinkel, Ursula Wild, Thomas C Erren, Philip Lewis
pmc-12517027.description: IntroductionThe teaching profession plays a crucial role in society. From educating and forming future generations to fulfilling various administrative tasks and managing expectations and experiences that reach beyond the classroom—teachers face immense demands on their time, energy, and emotional resources. Consequently, they are subject to high work burden.

pmc-12619738.title: Imatinib and blinatumomab successfully rescued a pediatric B-ALL patient with TERF2::PDGFRB fusion resistant to dasatinib and chemotherapy
pmc-12619738.creator: Fanghua Ye, Leyuan Wang, Yujie Qian, Wenjun Deng, Yan Yu, Liangchun Yang
pmc-12619738.description: PDGFRB-rearranged acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), an ABL-class Ph-like ALL subtype, typically exhibits chemotherapy resistance and poor prognosis. Precise diagnosis and therapies are crucial for improving outcomes. Here, we report a case of a 9-year-old male harboring a TERF2::PDGFRB fusion, exhibiting primary resistance to dasatinib, but achieving a remarkable response to imatinib.

pmc-13112920.title: Epidemiological and clinical characteristics of macrolide-resistant Bordetella pertussis in southern China: an 8-year retrospective study
pmc-13112920.creator: Zengrui Lin, Hongmei Wang, Cuijuan Liao, Guangcheng Deng, Jinjun Zheng, Ying Zhang, Xinxin Liu, Yuchun Long, Shufeng Tian, Biao Sun, Kun Tan, Jikui Deng
pmc-13112920.description: BackgroundRecently, macrolide-resistant Bordetella pertussis (MRBP) had emerged in China. The aim of this study was to evaluate the prevalence and clinical characteristics of MRBP in Shenzhen, southern China.MethodsWe enrolled patients with culture-confirmed pertussis at Shenzhen Children’s Hospital from January 2016 to December 2023. Demographic and clinical data of the patients were collected.

pmc-13247691.title: Improving case-finding of long-term health problems in disadvantaged communities: A Policy-focused Evidence Brief⋆
pmc-13247691.creator: Adnaan Ghanchi, Anita Patel, Helena Painter, Isla Kuhn, Anna Gkiouleka, Ian Holdroyd, Danielle Lamb, John Ford
pmc-13247691.description: Current challengesCase finding, which actively identifies undiagnosed conditions, is key to tackling the growing chronic disease burden, especially in disadvantaged groups. Diseases like type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease already cause millions of preventable deaths, with numbers rising due to aging populations, urbanization, and widening inequalities.

pmc-13373585.title: Intraperitoneal administertion: compatibility and stability of common antibiotics in amino acid-based peritoneal dialysate
pmc-13373585.creator: Bohua Zhang, Lichao Zhong, Xueli Zhou, Hui Zhong, Yuqin Xiong, Hongliu Yang, Ruoxi Liao
pmc-13373585.description: BackgroundThe preferred method of antibiotic administration for peritoneal dialysis-related peritonitis is intraperitoneal. However, there are few studies on the compatibility of antibiotics in amino acid-based peritoneal dialysate.MethodsOur study employed High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) and amino acid analyzer to evaluate the stability of different antibiotics in amino acid-based peritoneal dialysate.

pmc-13374492.title: Convergent evolution through independent rearrangements in the primate amylase locus
pmc-13374492.creator: Charikleia Karageorgiou, Petar Pajic, Stefan Ruhl, Omer Gokcumen
pmc-13374492.description: SUMMARYStructurally complex genomic regions can foster evolutionary convergence by repeatedly generating gene duplications that yield similar expression patterns and traits across lineages. Focusing on the primate amylase locus, we leveraged high-quality genome assemblies from 53 primate species and multi-tissue transcriptomes from Old World monkeys to reconstruct the evolutionary history of recurrent duplications.

pmc-13388639.title: From Lévy walks to Brownian motion in schools of zebrafish (Danio rerio)
pmc-13388639.creator: Andreza M da Silva, Francisco C B Leal, Pabyton G Cadena, Viviane M de Oliveira, Adauto J F de Souza, Antonio R de C Romaguera, Anderson L R Barbosa
pmc-13388639.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Population density strongly affects the internal organization and movement dynamics of fish schools. Here, we investigate density-dependent collective motion in zebrafish (Danio rerio) schools with group sizes ranging from 2 to 30 individuals. Using trajectories measured relative to the school center of mass, we show that individual motion is superdiffusive at low densities and progressively approaches Brownian-like behavior as density increases.

pmc-13423062.creator: Tareq Nafea Alharby, Muteb Alanazi, Mukhtar Ansari, Ali Felaih Almutairy, Osama Ayed Altamimi, Saud Talal Jaafari, Saleh Abdulwahab Alassaf, Meshari Khalid Altuwayhir, Faisal Nasser Almutiri, Fahad Saad Aljohani, Yaser Mohammed Al-Worafi, Yaser Mohammed Al-Worafi, Yaser Mohammed Al-Worafi

pmc-13453403.title: Mechanical Ptosis as the Initial Presentation of Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis
pmc-13453403.creator: Roberto Ramirez Hernandez, Dominguez-Salgado LA, Angel Nava Castañeda
pmc-13453403.description: BackgroundEosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare ANCA-associated small-vessel vasculitis that may involve the orbit. Dacryoadenitis presenting as unilateral mechanical ptosis is an unusual ophthalmic manifestation that may mimic inflammatory or neoplastic orbital disease.Case PresentationA 68-year-old man presented with unilateral eyelid swelling and lacrimal gland enlargement associated with orbital inflammation. Orbital imaging demonstrated dacryoadenitis.

pmc-13607628.title: Parenteral Treprostinil as an Effective Bridge to Lung Transplant in Patients with Severe Pulmonary Hypertension Associated with Interstitial Lung Disease
pmc-13607628.creator: Jennifer Hopkins, Shameek Gayen
pmc-13607628.description: Pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Lung transplantation remains the definitive therapy for selected patients; however, severe pulmonary vascular dysfunction and hemodynamic instability may complicate transplant candidacy and pre-transplant management. The role of parenteral prostacyclin therapy as a bridge to transplantation in this population remains poorly defined.

pmc-13673568.title: Chamber‐Specific Morphometry and Quantitative Cardiac Histology in the Broad‐Snouted Caiman (Caiman latirostris)
pmc-13673568.creator: Maria Eduarda Natal Nascimento, Gabriela Nogueira Maggio, Maysa Barbosa de Almeida, Caio Rafael Siqueira Vasconcelos, Vinícius José da Silva Cardoso de Brito, Arianne Pontes Oriá, Fernanda Gosuen Gonçalves Dias, Marcela Aldrovani Rodrigues
pmc-13673568.description: Quantitative cardiac morphology remains poorly documented in crocodilians. Hearts from four commercially reared male Caiman latirostris were examined by gross morphometry, histology, stereology, reticulin staining and Masson's trichrome. Relative heart mass averaged 0.125% of body mass. The left ventricular wall was numerically thicker than the right.
